name: Blood-Born (S-Class Veritus Champion Sanguine Bond)
body:
The blood-born are veritus champions whose power manifested early in life, causing them to suffer as they were thrust out of the normal life they led. Most grew into spiteful adults, shunned by those who didn’t understand the gifts they themselves were not yet able to fully grasp.

Form Blood Blade (Su)

At 4th level, a blood-born veritus champion can convert 4 points from his blood debt to create or reshape a weapon only he can wield as a move action. The champion must choose the form of his blood blade at 4th level. He can either form it into a light weapon, a one-handed weapon, or a two-handed weapon sized for him. Once chosen, his blood blade stays in this form every time the champion forms his blood blade (the listed values are for medium weapons).

One or two light weapons that each deal 1d6 damage.
The one-handed weapon deals 1d8 damage.
The two-handed weapon deals 2d6 damage.

In all forms, the blood blade has a critical threat range of 19-20/x2. A blood-born champion with powerful build or any similar ability forms an appropriately-sized blood blade dealing the size-appropriate amount of damage.

Regardless of the weapon form the champion has chosen, his blood blade does not have a set damage type. When shaping his weapon and assigning abilities to it, the blood-born chooses whether it will deal bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. The blood-born may change the damage type of an existing blood blade, or may summon a new blood blade with a different damage type, as a full-round action; otherwise, the blood blade retains the last damage type chosen every time it is summoned.

A blood blade can be broken (it has hardness 10 and 10 hit points); however, the champion can simply create another on his next move action. The moment he relinquishes his grip on his blade, it dissipates (unless he intends to throw it; see below). A blood blade is considered a magic weapon for the purpose of overcoming Damage Reduction and is considered a masterwork weapon.

In places where magic or psionic effects do not normally function (such as within an antimagic field), the champion can attempt to sustain his blood blade by making a DC 20 Will save. On a successful save, the blood-born maintains his blood blade for a number of rounds equal to his veritus champion level before he needs to check again, although the blood blade is treated for all purposes as a non-magical, masterwork weapon while in a place where magic and psionic effects do not normally function. On an unsuccessful attempt, the blood blade vanishes. As a move action on his turn, the blood-born can attempt a new Will save to rematerialize his blood blade while he remains within the effect. He gains a bonus on Will saves made to maintain or form his blood blade equal to the total enhancement bonus of his blood blade (see below).

The blood-born chooses the appearance of his blood blade, although its shape must reflect the selections the blood-born has chosen: a bludgeoning blood blade would be blunt, slashing would have an edge, etc.

Shape Blood Blade: The blood-born’s blood blade retains the last chosen form every time it is formed until the blood-born reshapes it. If the blood-born chooses to reshape his blade, it requires a full-round action to do so. He may also re-assign the type of damage dealt as part of reshaping his blood blade if he so chooses. The champion can reassign the ability or abilities he has added to his blood blade; see below. To do so, he must first spend 8 hours in concentration. These cannot be the normal 8 hours used for rest, even if the blood-born does not require sleep. After that period, the blood blade materializes with the new ability or abilities selected by the blood-born.

This ability replaces blood magic.

Throw Blood Blade (Ex)

At 6th level, a blood-born veritus champion can throw his blood blade. Light weapon mind blades have a range increment of 20 ft. One-handed weapon mind blades have a range increment of 15 ft. Two-handed weapon mind blades cannot be thrown without the Two-Handed Throw blade skill. Whether or not the attack hits, a thrown mind blade then dissipates.

This ability replaces waves of blood.

Enhance Blood Blade (Su)

At 8th, 12th, 16th, and 20th level, a blood-born veritus champion’s blood blade gains a +1 enhancement bonus when formed. This stacks with similar bonuses, such as those from sheathed in blood, up to a total +5 bonus.

In addition, the blood-born can select any magic weapon special ability when spending enhancement bonuses from either ability, up to a total combined bonus of +1 per two veritus champion levels.

This ability replaces sanguine step.

Blade Skill

At 10th, 14th, and 18th level, a blood-born veritus champion gains a blade skill for which he qualifies as a soulknife of his veritus champion level. A sample list of blade skills can be found here. The blood-born also qualifies for the Extra Blade Skill feat.

This ability replaces blood possession.

Alter Blade (Ex)

The blood-born gains the ability to shape his blood blade into different weapon forms. He may change his blade’s form to the light weapon, one-handed weapon, or two-handed weapon forms any time he forms his blood blade. Additionally, the blood-born may choose to form his blood blade into a one-handed weapon and a light weapon instead of two light weapons.

Blade Rush (Ex)

As a swift action, the blood-born can convert 12 points of his blood debt and move up to his speed without provoking attacks of opportunity.

Blade Rush Frenzy (Ex)

The blood-born can convert 12 points of his blood debt as a full-round action to move up to his speed without provoking attacks of opportunity and make a single melee attack against each creature he is adjacent to at any point in his movement. Each attack is made at his highest base attack bonus with a –2 penalty on the attack roll. The blood-born must possess the Blade Rush blade skill in order to select this blade skill.

Deadly Blow (Ex)

The blood-born’s blood blade critical multiplier increases by 1.
